validation.notes: Ran from the workspace root with Node v24.14.0; all 10 scenarios passed and the process exited 0. The script loads the real submitted modules (project-trust.ts, resource-loader.ts, settings-manager.ts) through .prale-eval/subject.mjs, with only in-memory settings storage, extension loading, package resolution and trust UI/extension boundaries faked, and asserts: (1) a headless reload with no stored decision and ask policy resolves to deny; (2) stored decisions, --trust overrides, never/always policies, interactive approval (no persistence for approve-once) and a remembered extension decision are honored; (3) SettingsManager.setProjectTrusted(false) immediately empties getProjectSettings() and falls merged values back to global settings; (4) a resolver-driven reload denies and resolves only CLI + global extensions, with neither bootstrap nor final resolves ever seeing trusted=true; (5) approval makes project configuration and the project extension visible, and a reload without a resolver retains both trust and resources without re-prompting; (6) revocation via a stored denial after an earlier approval clears project settings, drops the project extension from the next resolved set while keeping global and CLI extensions and global compaction values, and a later resolver-less reload keeps the revoked state; (7) revocation via an explicit trustOverride=false behaves the same. Mutation check: each of the three production files was restored alone to its faulty baseline (project-trust.ts hasUI => true, settings-manager.ts projectSettings = projectSettings, resource-loader.ts setProjectTrusted(true)) and the script failed with an explicit AssertionError in every case (exit 1, no import error, boundary error or timeout): 'missing UI must fail closed, not imply consent', 'revocation must clear cached project configuration', and 'headless ask reload must leave the project untrusted' respectively; the repair was restored and the run passed again. No temporary inputs were needed: all state is in-memory inside the subject helper, and scratch files used during development were deleted. Dependency-based repo suites (vitest/tsgo) were not run because node_modules is not installed and installing dependencies is out of scope; validation uses only Node 24 built-ins.
